answer: In a decentralized agent economy, resisting Sybil attacks relies on game-theoretic multi-agent auditing paired with topological cut verifications. Auditing agents inspect transaction subgraphs to isolate any clustered partition—whether traversing an isolated oasis of activity, navigating a disputed lagoon of accounts, or extinguishing a malicious ember before it spreads. When cross-cluster topological cuts reveal artificially inflated trust metrics, validators trigger stake slashing, imposing a superlinear cost on the attacker as forged identities multiply.
